security.title: Security
security.subtitle: Two-factor authentication (TOTP) for your account.
security.requireMfaTitle: Require two-factor authentication for everyone in this workspace
security.requireMfaSubtitle: Owner-only. When on, anyone who hasn't set up MFA is redirected to enroll before they can use the app — a correct password alone won't sign them in.
security.requireDeviceChallengeSubtitle: Owner-only. When on, a correct password from a browser we haven't seen before requires confirming a code emailed to the account, once per device. Skipped for accounts that already have MFA enabled.
security.kmsSubtitle: Owner-only. Every secret this platform stores is encrypted by default under our own managed key. Registering your own cloud KMS key here is a real config change, but the actual encrypt/decrypt calls to your cloud provider are not yet wired in this build — see docs/FEATURES.md §11.1.
security.kmsKeyReferencePlaceholder: Key ARN / Vault URI / resource name
security.kmsExternalProviderNotice: This registers your key reference, but this build cannot yet actually call out to your cloud provider's KMS API — disclosed limitation, not a silent fallback.
security.scanPrompt: Scan this into your authenticator app, or enter the secret manually, then confirm with a generated code.
security.recoveryCodesShownOnce: Recovery codes — store these now, they won't be shown again. Each can be used once in place of a code if you lose access to your authenticator app.
security.disablePrompt: Confirm your password and a current code to disable two-factor authentication.
security.sessionsExplainer: Signing out a session takes effect immediately here and on any future request to this service. It does not instantly revoke that session's token on other parts of the platform — those recognize it as valid until it naturally expires (within an hour).
security.passkeysExplainer: Phishing-resistant sign-in via Touch ID, Windows Hello, or a security key. Registering a passkey enables two-factor authentication for your account, the same as an authenticator app.
security.passkeyRegisterFailed: Couldn't add that passkey — verification failed or the prompt was cancelled.

myApprovals.title: My approvals
myApprovals.empty: No approval requests addressed to you.

portfolio.title: Portfolio
portfolio.subtitle: Every project's real cost report, summed — not a duplicated computation, the same numbers each project's own Budget page shows.

projectMembers.title: Project members
projectMembers.subtitle: Every tenant member already sees every project. This screen only matters for guests — a guest sees ONLY the projects they're added to here.
projectMembers.inviteGuestExplainer: Creates a new account scoped to no project by default — they're added to THIS project automatically once invited.
projectMembers.empty: No explicit members — every non-guest tenant member can still see this project.

goals.title: Goals
goals.subtitle: A single target number with a progress bar — no Objective/Key-Result ceremony. For business-outcome tracking with automatic epic rollup, see OKRs.

forms.title: Forms
forms.subtitle: A form whose submission creates a real ticket. Public forms need no login — share the link with anyone.

mfaSetup.title: Set up two-factor authentication
mfaSetup.subtitle: This workspace requires MFA for every account. Finish enrollment to continue.
mfaSetup.scanPrompt: Scan this into your authenticator app, or enter the secret manually, then confirm with a generated code.
mfaSetup.recoveryCodesShownOnce: Save these recovery codes now — they're shown only once.

publicForm.thanksBody: Your submission was recorded as ticket #{ticketNumber}.
publicForm.noRequests: No requests found for that email.

notificationPreferences.title: Notification preferences
notificationPreferences.subtitle: Mute a category of push notification everywhere — off by default means unchanged, no row means enabled.
notificationPreferences.digestSubtitle: Opt in to a rollup email of your notifications instead of (or alongside) push. Off by default.

notificationScheme.title: Notification scheme
notificationScheme.subtitle: Project-level default for who gets notified on standard ticket events. Distinct from each person's own mute preference, and independent of any automation rules configured for this project.

automations.title: Automations
automations.subtitle: Generic “when X then Y” rules. Fires on real ticket events (created, status change, assignment), plus one time-based trigger (unassigned for N hours) checked hourly by the platform scheduler.
automations.trigger_stale_unassigned: Ticket has been unassigned for N hours
automations.toStatePlaceholder: To state (optional, e.g. “Done” — leave blank to match any)

views.title: Views
views.subtitle: The same tickets, four ways — pick a saved query, then a view type.

pulls.noSuggestedReviewers: No blame-based reviewer suggestions for this PR (new files with no prior history on the target branch).

settings.permissionsSubtitle: Manage who has owner/admin access to this workspace. Only an owner can change roles, and no one can change their own.
settings.serviceHooksSubtitle: Deliver a signed webhook to an external URL when platform events happen.
settings.secretShownOnce: Signing secret — store this now, it won't be shown again:
settings.branchProtectionSubtitle: Require reviews before a pull request can merge into a protected branch.
settings.branchAllowlistSubtitle: Explicit per-branch merge allowlist — beyond CODEOWNERS/review-count rules. Unrestricted until at least one entry exists for a matching pattern.
settings.emptyBranchAllowlist: No allowlist entries — every branch is unrestricted (fail-open).
settings.activitySubtitle: A read-only, append-only log of security-relevant events across this workspace.
settings.chainValid: Chain verified — all {count} entries intact, no tampering detected.
settings.connectorsSubtitle: Install and sync third-party connectors — a small marketplace on top of the public API/webhooks story.
settings.customRolesExplainer: Grant a member a narrow, specific capability without making them an admin. Owners and admins already have every permission.

artifacts.title: Artifacts
artifacts.subtitle: A real npm-registry-protocol-compatible package feed. Publish with a real npm client (npm publish --registry=<this>) — there's no publish form here, same as every real package registry.

ticketDetail.devPanelEmpty: No linked commits or pull requests yet. Reference this ticket key (e.g. in a commit message or PR title) to link it here.

ticketTemplates.title: Ticket templates
ticketTemplates.subtitle: Pre-filled title/description/type for common ticket shapes.

releases.title: Releases
releases.emptyNotes: No tickets tagged to this release yet.

dependencyGraph.title: Dependency graph
dependencyGraph.subtitle: Every Blocks/Duplicates/Relates To link between tickets in this project, in one view.
dependencyGraph.empty: No linked tickets yet — add a link from a ticket's detail page.
dependencyGraph.criticalPathCycle: This graph has a cycle in its “blocks” links — critical path can't be computed until it's resolved.
dependencyGraph.criticalPathEmpty: No “blocks” links yet — critical path only follows real blocking dependencies.

deliveryPlans.title: Delivery plans
deliveryPlans.subtitle: A saved, cross-project sprint timeline — pick projects, see every one of their sprints on one shared timeline.
deliveryPlans.unscheduledSubtitle: These sprints have no start/end date set, so they can't be plotted on the timeline.
deliveryPlans.emptyLanes: No sprints in the selected projects yet.
deliveryPlans.autoScheduleSubtitle: Computes suggested epic dates from team velocity, epic size, and blocking dependencies — a preview, never written until you apply it.
deliveryPlans.autoScheduleEmpty: No epics in this plan's projects yet.
deliveryPlans.autoScheduleApply: Apply — write these dates to each epic's due date
deliveryPlans.autoScheduleApplyConfirm: This overwrites each listed epic's due date with the computed end date. Continue?
deliveryPlans.velocityLabel: Assuming {points} points/sprint, {days}-day sprints (computed from recent completed sprints; override via the API for what-if scenarios).

pipelinesLibrary.title: Pipelines library
pipelinesLibrary.subtitle: Reusable pipeline config, referenced by name from a pipeline's YAML (variableGroups / secureFiles / a step's taskGroup) and resolved by the runner at execute time.
pipelinesLibrary.secureFilesSubtitle: Content is write-only — it's never returned once uploaded, only materialized into a run's workspace by the runner.
pipelinesLibrary.taskGroupsSubtitle: A named, reusable step sequence — a pipeline step references it via taskGroup: <name> instead of inlining run.

runners.title: Self-hosted runners
runners.subtitle: Register an external agent (on-prem, GPU, or otherwise) to run pipeline steps tagged runsOn: <label>.
runners.tokenShownOnce: Copy this token now — it won't be shown again. Set it as RUNNER_TOKEN when starting the agent.
runners.labelsHint: Comma-separated labels a pipeline step's runsOn: field matches against.

network.title: Network access
network.subtitle: Restrict login to specific IP addresses or CIDR ranges. Empty list = unrestricted.
network.unrestrictedNotice: No restrictions configured — anyone with valid credentials can log in from any network.
network.enforcedNotice: Login is restricted to the network ranges listed below.
network.geoRestrictionsSubtitle: Owner-only. Comma-separated ISO country codes (e.g. US, GB, AU). Empty = unrestricted. Note: this build's GeoIP resolver is a disclosed stub covering only IANA's documentation IP ranges — see docs/FEATURES.md §11.1.

budget.title: Budget & cost report
budget.uncostedNotice: {minutes} minutes logged by users with no rate card set — excluded from the dollar total above.

vendorSpend.title: Vendor & subscription spend
vendorSpend.subtitle: Track what this tenant pays third-party SaaS vendors, distinct from your own platform subscription.

search.title: Search
search.subtitle: Semantic search across tickets, wiki pages, and chat messages — one query, every source at once.
search.fallbackEmbeddingWarning: No embeddings API configured — using a deterministic dev-only fallback that is not real semantic search.

timesheets.title: Timesheet Approval & Contractor Invoicing
timesheets.subtitle: Approve submitted timesheets, then generate a real client invoice from the approved hours.

okrs.title: Objectives & Key Results
okrs.subtitle: Company objectives, with key results that either track a manual number or roll up automatically from a linked Epic.

dataRetention.title: Data Retention & Purge Policies
dataRetention.subtitle: Configured retention/backup policies per data class. Retention purges and DR backups both run on a real hourly/daily scheduler now, and can also be triggered on demand below — only the classes marked enforceable/automated actually do anything when triggered.
dataRetention.verifySucceeded: Restore verified — {count} row(s) successfully restored to a staging table (never touched live data).

platformOps.title: Platform Health & Cost Observability
platformOps.subtitle: Real-time uptime and memory usage polled directly from every service's own /health endpoint — the platform operator's view of what running all 17 services actually costs, not tenant-facing billing.

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.subtitle: Configure OIDC or SAML 2.0 so your organization can sign in through your identity provider.
sso.oidcExplainer: Authorization-code flow against any standards-compliant IdP (Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace).
sso.samlExplainer: SP-initiated flow. Paste your IdP's metadata XML below, then give the SP details underneath to your IdP admin.
sso.spDetailsHeading: Service provider details (give these to your IdP)

divisions.title: Divisions
divisions.subtitle: Sub-tenants of your organization — each fully isolated, with its own data, users, and settings.

flowMetrics.title: Flow metrics
flowMetrics.subtitle: Control chart (cycle time per completed ticket), cumulative flow (work-in-progress by state over time), and sprint burnup.

workflow.title: Workflow logic
workflow.subtitle: Conditions, validators, and post functions bound to each transition.

assets.title: Asset management
assets.subtitle: A queryable registry of hardware, software licenses, and servers — distinct from the one-time provisioning-task logs.

problems.title: Problem management
problems.subtitle: Root-cause tracking, distinct from incident response — one problem can span many recurring incidents.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.subtitle: Epic-level Gantt timeline — bars span from each epic's creation date to its due date; overdue and incomplete epics show in red.
roadmap.emptyScheduled: No epics with a due date set yet — set one on an epic, or use auto-scheduling on a delivery plan to compute one.
roadmap.unscheduledSubtitle: These epics can't be plotted on the timeline until a due date is set.

workflowDesigner.title: Workflow designer
workflowDesigner.subtitle: Drag states to arrange them. Click two states in sequence to add a transition between them.
workflowDesigner.linkHint: Click the state this transition should lead to (or click the same state again to cancel).
workflowDesigner.deleteStateConfirm: Delete state "{name}"? This is only possible if no ticket is currently in it.
workflowDesigner.instructions: Drag a state to reposition it. Click a state, then click another to create a transition between them. Click a transition's label to delete it. Click the × on a state to delete it.

customFields.title: Custom fields
customFields.subtitle: Typed fields, scoped to issue types, arranged per create/edit screen.
customFields.noApplicableFields: No fields apply to this issue type yet.
